forecasts.reference-class: US airline/telecom infrastructure company undergoing a financially backed, all-cash merger with a large acquirer and a defined closing horizon, with no near-term debt maturities (Frontier Group Holdings during Verizon acquisition in 2026).

sources.claim: Verizon to acquire Frontier in an all-cash transaction valued at $20 billion; closing expected in approximately 18 months (by early 2026).
Frontier stockholders approved the acquisition; closing expected by the first quarter of 2026.
Regulatory approvals received; closing expected to occur on January 20, 2026.
Frontier reports liquidity of approximately $2.3 billion as of June 30, 2025, with no near-term debt maturities before 2027.
CNBC reports Verizon to acquire Frontier for $20 billion; closing expected by 2026.
Spirit Airlines rejects Frontier's takeover bid; Spirit continues standalone bankruptcy restructuring.
Spirit Airlines announces standalone recapitalization and rejects Frontier's latest proposal.
Spirit Airlines rejects Frontier merger; Spirit aims to emerge from bankruptcy according to its plan.
Baron's coverage discusses Spirit–Frontier merger talks in the context of bankruptcy dynamics.
BTS data show US airlines posting losses in 2024, illustrating sector-wide financial stress that informs bankruptcy risk context.
NBER study on airline bankruptcies shows bankruptcies occur during weak demand and can affect service levels.

Frontier Group Holdings reports total available liquidity of $874 million as of December 31, 2025 and states it expects to meet cash requirements for the next twelve months using cash, undrawn revolver, and cash flows.
As of March 31, 2025 Frontier had no outstanding borrowings under its Revolving Loan Facility, with $205 million undrawn, and disclosed debt maturities totaling about $512 million due 2026–2030.
Frontier reported Q4 2024 results with end-2024 liquidity of $935 million, indicating substantial liquidity at year-end 2024.
Altman Z-Score for ULCC (Frontier Group Holdings) is around 0.38, placing it in a distress zone and implying elevated bankruptcy risk per the model.
ChartMill shows an Altman-Z score around 0.39 for ULCC, also indicating distress.
